archetype: Naya Dinosaur critical-mass deck whose currency is a Dinosaur ENTERING rather than a creature attacking: Gishath's combat-damage reveal is the batch entry-maker, and V5 rebuilt the layer that cashes an entry into damage (Purphoros) and into a second entry (Molten Echoes), so the deck now has a noncombat clock that runs at all three seats and a combat clock that runs at one. Commander-RELIANT, not merely built around the commander. Bracket floor 3 on two Game Changers (Enlightened Tutor, Worldly Tutor) and zero contained combos.

role_assignment.default_role: CONTROL POSTURE until the first entry-payoff resolves, then BEATDOWN — and V5 moved where that line falls. strategy:whos-the-beatdown's operational test is inevitability: "whoever loses the long game must be the beatdown". Before V5 the deck owned the long game only once Gishath connected, because every payoff was priced in combat damage at one seat. Purphoros changes the answer: it is an each-opponent drain, and strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry names exactly that class as the one that scales — "wide alpha strikes, loops, commander-damage kills, and each-opponent drains are the payoffs that actually scale" against "~120 combined life behind three defenses". So the honest reading is now split: you are the CONTROL deck for the mana climb (goldfish, 10,000 iterations, seed 42, sha 80701018: mean available mana 3.368 at turn 3, 6.043 at turn 6, 7.666 at turn 8; 'Ramp or fixing drawn' 91.0% assembled, 74.3% by turn 6, mean turn 3.106), and you become the BEATDOWN the moment an entry engine is on the battlefield, not the moment the 7/6 is. strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection is the posture that buys the climb — "experienced tables hit the quiet ramp player", and captain's log 001 is the record of the table getting the tiers wrong in your favour: "They spent their wraths on mid-tier dinosaurs and had nothing left when the commander landed." Expect that to be a one-time gift, not a plan. Role is seat-relative per the same section's Commander correction: against the seat Purphoros is draining you are the beatdown from the turn it lands; against the seat holding a sweeper you are still the control deck.
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: Two triggers now, and they are different events. (1) THE COMBAT PIVOT, unchanged: a resolved Gishath plus a way to make the hit land — Kinjalli's Sunwing already tapping their blockers, Rogue's Passage-style evasion is NOT in this list, so realistically a trample swing into a board you have already shrunk — with a protection instant held. strategy:pivot-point: "hold the protection spell for the turn you commit, not after", and strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window sets the bar the table applies to you: "assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing." Flawless Maneuver is the only shield castable for nothing on the turn you tap out for eight (oracle text). Goldfish: commander cast median turn 7, mean 7.278, 26.7% by turn 6, never by turn 10 in 2,298 of 10,000 games. (2) THE ENTRY PIVOT, new in V5: Purphoros resolved plus any repeatable source of entries. This one does not need a combat step, does not need the commander, and does not open your defences — which is precisely what strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window prefers, a "win attempt [that] either can't be profitably answered ... or doesn't need to resolve fully to leave you ahead." Captain's log 002 is the cost of missing the pivot on the combat side: '8-9 dinos with counters, 30+ power on board ... Should have swung everything at both.' strategy:combat-math.racing names the same rule — "the moment you stabilize, flip to offense to shrink the window in which they can draw out of it."

engines.engine: THE PUT DOOR, in batches. Reveal cards equal to combat damage, put every Dinosaur among them onto the battlefield. The 99 holds 28 Dinosaurs (29 counting the commander, who is in the command zone and can never be revealed), so a 7-damage connect expects 7 x 28/99 = 1.98 free entries; the goldfish measures 2.02 (4.08 bodies over 2.016 fires). Nothing gated on 'if you cast it' fires through this door.
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); goldfish_metrics.commander_reveal, declared, fired in 7,300 of 10,000 games, mean_fired 2.016, mean_bodies 4.08, at a connect rate of 0.70/attack read from Forge run sythis-enchantress-vs-jarad-graveyard-vs-abaddon-n40-432faa65; deck-facts counts (91 entries, 100 copies)

engines.engine: ENTRY -> DAMAGE, at every seat, with your own board untouched. 2 damage to each opponent per other creature entering, tokens included. At the measured 2.02 entries per connect that is ~4 damage per opponent per connect and ~12 across a three-opponent table, before the entries that come from casting, from Ghalta and Mavren's attack tokens and from Molten Echoes. This is the V5 change that makes the deck's clock scale with the table rather than with one defender.
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); arithmetic over goldfish_metrics.commander_reveal.mean_bodies / mean_fired; engine.json conversion stage (sha 80701018c37d)

engines.piece: Purphoros over Chandra's Ignition (the swap, enumerated)
engines.engine: A ONE-SHOT RESET TRADED FOR A REPEATABLE CLOCK. I enumerated the counterfactual from cards.json rather than asserting it: Ignition aimed at Gishath deals 7 to each other creature, and of the 34 other creature entries in this 99, 31 have toughness 7 or less. Only Ghalta and Mavren (12/12), Ghalta, Primal Hunger (12/12) and Zacama, Primal Calamity (9/9) survive on toughness; Huatli, Poet of Unity is a 2/3 on her front face and dies. One refinement the brief did not carry: Purphoros itself is INDESTRUCTIBLE, so it is inside the 31-by-toughness and would in fact survive — the card that replaced Ignition is the one card Ignition could not have killed. strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry is the frame: 'Your cards should do something to all three seats or win the game', and a symmetrical sweeper in a deck whose plan is a wide board does something to YOU.
engines.evidence: cards.json toughness enumeration (34 other creature entries, 31 with toughness <= 7, 3 above); oracle text for Purphoros (indestructible)

engines.engine: ENTRY -> SECOND ENTRY, and the card that splits the deck's free-entry effects into two classes. Name Dinosaur: every NONTOKEN Dinosaur that enters makes a hasty copy exiled at the next end step. engine.json enumerates the payoff from cards.json rather than assuming it — 10 Dinosaurs in the deck carry an entry trigger, 8 of them fire on the copy, and Zacama, Primal Calamity and Wakening Sun's Avatar do NOT, both being gated on 'if you cast it'. 7 of the 29 Dinosaur cards are legendary, so their copy dies to the legend rule at once: the trigger resolves, the body does not stay. The copies are tokens and so do not re-trigger Molten Echoes, and do not trigger a payoff worded 'nontoken'.
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); engine.json conversion stage enumeration, sha 80701018c37d

engines.piece: CAST doors vs PUT doors (the structural distinction)
engines.engine: A real strategic split, not trivia. CAST doors — Descendants' Path's upkeep free cast, Pantlaza's discover, World War Hulk chapter I's free red-or-green creature spell, Hunting Velociraptor's prowl {2}{R} — fire everything that listens for a cast, including Zacama's land untap, Wakening Sun's Avatar's one-sided wipe and Up the Beanstalk's draw on mana value 5 or greater. PUT doors — Gishath's reveal, Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual, Savage Order — fire only entry triggers. Route your two 'if you cast it' bombs through the first class deliberately; they are dead weight off the second. strategy:tempo.sequencing's first rule applies directly: 'think through the entire turn before doing anything', because which door you use decides which half of your board text exists.
engines.evidence: oracle text for Zacama, Wakening Sun's Avatar, Descendants' Path, Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual // Zoological Study, Savage Order, World War Hulk, Hunting Velociraptor, Up the Beanstalk (cards.json); engine.json fuel + conversion stages

engines.engine: ENTRY -> CARD, once a turn: discover X where X is the entering creature's toughness. It is the enhancer tier of strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density's 'Nicol asks 7-8 enablers and 10-12 enhancers against ~25 standalone cards' — a payoff that does nothing alone and multiplies every entry the reveal makes. The once-a-turn clause caps it at one discover per reveal batch, which is why it is an enhancer and not a second engine.
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); engine.json conversion stage; goldfish target 'Dinosaur payoff drawn (per-dino trigger engine)' 85.6% assembled, 61.5% by turn 6, mean turn 3.942

engines.engine: A PUT-door tutor: sacrifice a creature with power 4 or greater, search a Dinosaur straight onto the battlefield with indestructible until your next turn. strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors prices what that buys — a tutor is 'essentially an additional copy of any card in our deck' — and the sacrifice is the tempo cost the same section names: 'the more tutors you play, the less actual cards you get to play'. It is the only card in the 99 that sacrifices a creature (engine.json enumerated this: six fetches and two Sagas sacrifice themselves and nothing else does), so the deck has no sacrifice-outlet redundancy and this line is never repeatable.
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); engine.json fuel stage enumeration

engines.engine: DAMAGE FLOOR: 'If a source would deal damage to another Dinosaur you control, prevent all but 1.' It converts the deck's own damage into exactly 1 — which is what makes Blasphemous Act one-sided, and what turns Savage Stomp's fight into a 1-damage enrage trigger rather than a trade. It is not 'another Dinosaur' to itself, so the Act kills it. This is strategy:card-advantage.virtual's mechanism, not a card-draw one: 'a card that blanks several opposing cards generates advantage without drawing anything.'
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); stacks/004-wrathful-blasphemous-temple.json, checker.verdict == pass, is the only VERIFIED line in this deck touching Altisaur

engines.piece: Savage Stomp, Itzquinth, Triumphant Chomp, Trumpeting Carnosaur (discard mode), Zacama {2}{R}
engines.engine: SELF-DAMAGE SOURCES, the answer to captain's log 002's complaint that 'Enrage engine in Gishath is idling - too few ping sources to activate it'. engine.json enumerated every card in the 99 that can mark damage on your own Dinosaur without spending an answer on yourself and found six, not one: Blasphemous Act, Savage Stomp, Itzquinth (its damage may be aimed at another creature you control), Triumphant Chomp, Trumpeting Carnosaur's discard mode and Zacama's {2}{R}. Savage Stomp is the V5 addition that matters structurally — {G} pointed at your own Dinosaur, a +1/+1 counter, and under Temple Altisaur exactly 1 damage taken. The enrage payoffs it feeds are Trapjaw Tyrant (exile a creature an opponent controls) and Wrathful Raptors (deal that much damage to any target that isn't a Dinosaur).
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); engine.json output stage, which explicitly overturns the previous model's claim that Blasphemous Act was the only such source; goldfish target 'Enrage engine drawn' 58.4% assembled, 28.7% by turn 6, mean turn 5.702

engines.engine: MASS RE-ENTRY, and with the V5 conversion layer down it is no longer only a dodge: the end-step return is a simultaneous entry of your whole board, which is a Purphoros trigger per creature and a Molten Echoes copy of every nontoken Dinosaur. strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math's instruction to 'buy resilience instead of restraint where you can' is exactly this card's job, and V5 turned the resilience purchase into an offensive one.
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); engine.json protection stage, sha 80701018c37d

engines.engine: THE ONLY FREE SHIELD on the turn you tap out for eight — 'If you control a commander, you may cast this spell without paying its mana cost.' strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance prices the alternative: 'each return trip to the command zone adds {2} per prior command-zone cast ... and, the bigger price, a tempo turn spent re-casting instead of advancing.' Heroic Intervention (hexproof, covers targeting), Akroma's Will (protection from each colour), Boros Charm (indestructible, does not cover exile) and Eerie Interlude all cost mana the same turn.
engines.evidence: oracle text for all five (cards.json); deck-audit protection axis 8 copies against a 5-7 target, verdict OVER; goldfish target 'Protection held for the board' 71.7% assembled, 52.2% by turn 6

engines.piece: Bloom Tender, and the red mana problem
engines.engine: V5's mana pass fixed green and left RED as the binding colour. mana_analysis on-curve probability, lands only: W 0.831, G 0.764, R 0.548; with rocks and dorks W 0.866, G 0.822, R 0.610. That matters because the two cards V5 added to the conversion layer are red: Purphoros at {3}{R} and Molten Echoes at {2}{R}{R}. strategy:deckbuilding.mana-base.color-sources gives the budget — 'Double pip: ... 26 for 2{C}{C}' — and the deck has 21 red sources in total (19 lands, 2 nonland), five short for Molten Echoes on curve. Purphoros at a single pip on turn 4 wants 17 and has 21, so it clears. Bloom Tender does not help: its Vivid mana is one per colour among permanents you control, and mana_analysis records it as producing nothing.

engines.engine: THE WIDE ALPHA, the other payoff strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry names as scaling. Overwhelming Stampede gives +X/+X where X is your greatest power, which also makes Gishath's reveal that many cards wider; Ghalta and Mavren's attack trigger makes tokens, and under Purphoros a token entering is damage before blockers are even declared. Goldfish mean board power reaches 15.087 at turn 6 and 34.415 at turn 8 — against ONE opponent with no blockers, so a ceiling on speed.
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); goldfish_metrics.combat mean_board_power_by_turn, kill_by_turn_rate 0.609 at turn 8, mean_kill_turn 7.987, explicitly one opponent at 40 life with no blockers (goldfish model assumptions)

candidate_missing_lines.title: Gishath's reveal into Molten Echoes: how many entries does one connect actually make?
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Oracle text: the reveal PUTS Dinosaurs onto the battlefield, Molten Echoes triggers on each nontoken Dinosaur that enters and makes a hasty copy. The open questions a stack must settle are the ones a frame cannot: whether the batch enters simultaneously and how the triggers are ordered, whether the hasty copies can attack the same combat (they enter after combat damage, so almost certainly not this combat), whether Pantlaza's once-a-turn discover caps the batch at one, and what the legend rule does to a copy of one of the 7 legendary Dinosaurs. Nothing in this deck's five stacks covers Molten Echoes at all.

candidate_missing_lines.title: One connect, counted in damage: Purphoros triggers off a reveal batch
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Purphoros triggers on each OTHER creature entering and is an enchantment whose trigger does not require it to be a creature (devotion gates only whether it IS a creature). At the measured 2.02 entries per fire that is ~4 to each seat per connect, doubled if Molten Echoes is down. The arithmetic is the deck's whole new clock and no verified artifact states it; stack 001 (Gishath trigger cascade) predates both cards.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Eerie Interlude as an offensive spell: a whole board re-entering at end step
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Oracle text: exile any number of your creatures, return them at the beginning of the next end step. Each return is an entry, so every Purphoros and Molten Echoes trigger fires again. The rules questions worth citing are the ones this frame must not assert: whether the returns are simultaneous, how the copies and the once-a-turn discover interact, and whether the Molten Echoes tokens made this way survive to the exile clause at the NEXT end step.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Savage Stomp under Temple Altisaur as a one-mana repeatable enrage trigger
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Savage Stomp costs {2} less targeting a Dinosaur you control, so {G}; the fight marks damage on your own creature, and Temple Altisaur prevents all but 1 of it. That is a removal spell that also triggers enrage at a cost of one green mana. Stack 004 verifies the Blasphemous Act version of this interaction, not the Savage Stomp version, and Savage Stomp is a V5 addition.

candidate_missing_lines.title: World War Hulk chapter III as the Enlarge replacement: doubling Gishath's power for a 14-card reveal
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Chapter III doubles a creature's power and toughness until end of turn and grants trample. Captain's log 001 records the Enlarge version of exactly this line winning a game ('+7/+7 on Gishath, swinging for 14 ... Revealed 14 off that trigger'), and Enlarge was cut in V5. Whether the Saga's three-turn clock can be made to land on a connect turn is the strategic question; the timing is the rules question.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Zacama and Wakening Sun's Avatar arriving through a PUT door
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Both carry an 'if you cast it' gate — Zacama's land untap, the Avatar's destroy-all-non-Dinosaurs. Off Gishath's reveal, Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual or Savage Order the gate fails and only the body arrives. Zacama's three activated abilities still work, which makes it the deck's on-board answer suite regardless of how it arrived; that distinction is worth a citation because the handbook leans on it.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Re-verify the Gishath trigger cascade against the V5 conversion layer
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: stacks/001-gishath-trigger-cascade.json passes the checker, but it was written before Purphoros and Molten Echoes were in the list and therefore understates what a connect now produces. It is not wrong; it is incomplete. Regenerate rather than patch.

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: Still the worst frame, and V5 improved it in one specific way. strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math's instruction to 'deploy in waves' is structurally hard here because the commander's trigger IS the wave — a reveal that puts three Dinosaurs down is a commitment you did not get to size. What the section actually offers this deck is its other clause: 'buy resilience instead of restraint where you can — high toughness, indestructible and regeneration, token rebuilders, threats that replace themselves.' Purphoros is indestructible and survives a damage sweeper outright; Vaultborn Tyrant replaces itself on death; Carnage Tyrant cannot be targeted or countered; Eerie Interlude dodges a non-targeted mass exile and now returns the board as an offensive trigger batch. The rebuild price is the honest one from strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance: eight mana plus '{2} per prior command-zone cast'. Duke's rule in wrath-math is the discipline — 'commit exactly as much as wins before it arrives, no further' — and captain's log 002 records the pilot discovering it the hard way and the right way in the same game: 'In removal-heavy games, holding creatures back through wipe waves is a real strategy, not just an accident.' Let another player's board be the reason the wrath gets cast. Forge's V3 record (0.343 at standard-v3, 12 wins in 35 decided of 40 games, 4 truncated, run 432faa65 dated 2026-09-10) is on the PRE-V5 list and must not be read as evidence for any of this.
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Taxes hit an eight-drop hardest, and the three cost reducers (Otepec Huntmaster, Urza's Incubator, Knight of the Stampede) are the tax resilience — but read strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial's velocity warning first: 'recount your hand under the tax — a two-spell turn becoming a one-spell turn halves the engine.' The role is forced: 'you rarely own the long game under an assembling lock, so you are the beatdown, racing the lock's completion.' Name your outs early. Against an artifact or enchantment lock piece the deck has exactly two answers, and I enumerated them rather than counting a role tag: Zacama's {2}{G} (destroy target artifact or enchantment, activated, so instant speed once Zacama is down) and Bronzebeak Foragers' ETB (exile up to one target nonland permanent per opponent, until it leaves). Beast Within and Thrashing Brontodon, which covered this in V4, were both cut. deck-audit reads interaction-breadth 3 classes against a floor of 5 — artifact 1, enchantment 1, creature 9 — and names GRAVEYARD and LAND as the classes with no answer at all. strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite is the target: 'cover the classes — creature, artifact, enchantment, graveyard, land — before doubling any', and its stax clause is the sharp one: 'a counter answers a lock piece only on the way in, so some answers must be castable under the tax.' A {2}{G} activation on a resolved nine-drop is not castable under a tax you have not yet beaten. Against a Torpor Orb effect the reveal still puts bodies down but the entire V5 conversion layer goes dark — Purphoros, Molten Echoes and Pantlaza are all entry triggers. Plan on the trample swing, not on the entries. Unclaimed Territory cannot pay an activated ability (deck-facts restricted_mana); Secluded Courtyard can, because its clause says so.
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: The deck holds the ground with toughness rather than numbers — goldfish mean bodies 3.179 at turn 6 — and Temple Altisaur is the reason it holds at all: a damage floor of 1 on every other Dinosaur blanks small attackers wholesale, which is strategy:card-advantage.virtual's exact mechanism, 'A big blocker against an aggro deck turns their small creatures into dead cards.' Its Commander correction is the one that sizes it: 'virtual advantage triples — one tax or pillow-fort effect can blank attack plans from three players at once.' Kinjalli's Sunwing makes their creatures enter tapped, which blanks haste; Runic Armasaur (2/5) and Curious Altisaur (2/5) are bodies that block and draw. Take the control role here and be patient: strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock's Commander correction says 'four-player games trend long, so inevitability compounds — engines are the default winning plan', and this deck's engine out-scales an aggro curve. The trap strategy:combat-math names is the one to avoid: 'chump blocking early to save spendable points'. Spend life above the threshold; you have Temple Altisaur and, once Purphoros is down, a clock that does not need your creatures to survive combat at all.
matchup_frames.vs_combo: The worst structural matchup and the frame is short because the deck's tools are. strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy sets the bar — 'the bar is "ends the game or ends my deck's function," not "looks scary"' — and adds the clause that binds here: 'held answers rot — against combo, or lethal already on board, the last profitable moment is now.' The deck's instant-speed interaction is Path to Exile, Swords to Plowshares and Trumpeting Carnosaur's discard mode ({2}{R}, 3 damage to a creature or planeswalker); there are no counterspells and nothing that answers a noncreature combo piece at instant speed except a resolved Zacama's {2}{G}. goldfish 'interaction castable with mana to spare' is 0.332 at turn 6 and 0.438 at turn 8 — and the model casts everything it can afford every turn, so those are FLOORS for a pilot developing at full speed, not what a pilot choosing to hold up two mana would have. Against a combo table the plan is strategy:critical-mass's own defence, stated flatly: 'the deck's defense is speed, redundancy, and resilience, not answers.' Race. Captain's log 002 is the loss that says so — a drain-combo seat (Vito) won a game in which the Gishath board had 30+ power and lethal available on two seats. Bracket floor 3, zero contained combo lines in this 99 (deck-facts combos: contained 0), so you are the slower deck against anything at bracket 4.

distribution_notes: 91 entries / 100 copies, 35 land copies over 26 land entries, 65 nonland (deck-facts counts). Curve by entry: 6 at one, 8 at two, 17 at three, 10 at four, 11 at five, 6 at six, 2 at seven, 2 at eight, 2 at nine, 1 at twelve — modal mana value 3 against strategy:deckbuilding.curve's measured Commander shape ('the modal mana value at 2, with 15.7 two-drops and 15.4 three-drops in the average deck and only ~1.5 cards at mana value 8+'); this deck holds five cards at mana value 8 or more, one of which is the plan. The same section is the licence: 'unless the majority of your deck is mana ramp... you're probably only going to be able to cast ONE big-mana spell per game.' 35 creature entries, 29 of them Dinosaurs including the commander — so 28 Dinosaurs in the 99, which is the number that makes the reveal reliable. strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors prices that directly: '90% by ten cards seen costs about 20 copies', and 28 clears it. The commander is the opposite case, one copy in the command zone, which is why strategy:deckbuilding.archetype-selection's line lands — 'built around your commander is not reliant on it. A deck whose only payoff sits in the command zone hands three opponents one target'; V5 partly buys that back, since Purphoros and Molten Echoes are payoffs that do not need Gishath. deck-audit (sha 80701018c37d) against strategy:deckbuilding.ratios' Command Zone template ('36–38 lands, 10–12 ramp, 10 card draw, 10–12 targeted removal, 3–4 board wipes'): mana-base 35 UNDER by 1, ramp 13 OVER by 1, card-advantage 6 UNDER by 4 (with Earthshaker Dreadmaw, Jetmir's Garden, Rishkar's Expertise, Runic Armasaur and Vaultborn Tyrant named as doing the job uncounted), interaction 9 AT against Walser's floor of 8, sweepers 1 AT, protection 8 OVER, threat-density 3 AT, taplands 4 AT (Karsten 'caps pure taplands at about four'), consistency 0.901 AT, colour-sources UNDER by 15. The one axis worth reading as a real weakness is INTERACTION-BREADTH, 3 classes of 5, uncovered: graveyard and land. Note what that does and does not say — the brief's framing that the deck 'cannot remove a blocker' does not survive enumeration: Path to Exile, Swords to Plowshares, Triumphant Chomp, Savage Stomp, Trumpeting Carnosaur's discard mode, Itzquinth's ETB, Zacama's {2}{R}, Trapjaw Tyrant's enrage exile and Blasphemous Act all remove creatures, and deck-audit reads the removal COUNT as AT. What V5 lost is BREADTH and the mass reset: Austere Command and Beast Within out, one artifact answer and one enchantment answer left. Goldfish (10,000 iterations, seed 42, sha 80701018c37d, model_version 5496ad1975b1, commander reveal declared at Forge's 0.70 connects/attack): 'Ramp or fixing drawn' 91.0% / 74.3% by turn 6 / mean turn 3.106 — the REQUIRED component, and the caution is that at 0.910 the split it creates is near-degenerate; 'Cost reducer or cheat-into-play' 83.0% / 65.4% / 3.382; 'Dinosaur payoff' 85.6% / 61.5% / 3.942; 'Gishath connection kit' 81.1% / 61.2% / 3.641; 'Enrage engine' 58.4% / 28.7% / 5.702; 'Protection held' 71.7% / 52.2% / 3.878; 'THE ONE-SIDED APOCALYPSE (stack 004)' 9.1% / 2.1% / 7.681. Unassisted figures are quoted throughout on purpose: goldfish_library._target_met is type-blind and lets any cast tutor fill any missing any_of group without asking whether it could legally find a member, so the *_assisted figures are not trustworthy here. Commander cast mean turn 7.278, median 7, 26.7% by turn 6, never by turn 10 in 2,298 of 10,000. Kill by turn 8 0.609, mean kill turn 7.987, no kill by turn 10 in 9.0% — one opponent at 40 life with no blockers, so an optimistic clock and a pessimistic board. Opening hands: 77.2% of first sevens keepable, 0.276 mean mulligans, 82.8% can act by turn 3. Land-drop hit rate 0.901 at turn 3, 0.575 at turn 6. Mana: 19 W / 21 R / 30 G sources against deck-facts source targets G 36 / R 36 / W 22; on-curve lands only W 0.831 / G 0.764 / R 0.548. RED is the binding colour after V5's green audit, and the two new conversion cards are the red ones. Card draw is systematically understated: engine.json/goldfish name 9 cards that draw and model 3, with Curious Altisaur, Hunter's Insight, Jetmir's Garden, Runic Armasaur, Selvala and Vaultborn Tyrant unmodelled, and Etali, Hunter's Insight, Pugnacious Hammerskull and Sunfrill Imitator listed as combat effects the parser cannot read. FORGE HAS NEVER SEEN V5: the newest run (432faa65, 2026-09-10, 40 games, 0.343 decided win rate) is on a pre-swap list, so there is no win-rate evidence for Purphoros, Molten Echoes or any other V5 card.
key_tensions: AN EIGHT-MANA COMMANDER THAT MUST CONNECT, IN A DECK AT ONE ANSWER PER NONCREATURE CLASS. Median cast turn 7 (goldfish), and strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window's standard applied to you — 'assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal'. V5's real defence against this is not a better connect kit; it is Purphoros, a second clock that does not need a combat step at all.

THE REVEAL IS A COMMITMENT YOU DO NOT GET TO SIZE. strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math says 'commit exactly as much as wins before it arrives, no further', and Gishath's trigger puts an unsized batch onto the battlefield whether or not that is what the wrath math wanted. The mitigations are resilience purchases (Eerie Interlude, Vaultborn Tyrant, Carnage Tyrant, indestructible Purphoros), not restraint.

RED IS THE BINDING COLOUR AND V5 LEANED ON IT. Molten Echoes at {2}{R}{R} wants 26 sources by Karsten's double-pip column and the deck has 21; red reads 0.548 on-curve on lands alone against green's 0.764. The green audit fixed the colour that was complained about in captain's log 002 and the new strain is one the log has never seen.

CARD DRAW IS THE MEASURED SHORTFALL AND IT IS PARTLY AN INSTRUMENT PROBLEM. deck-audit reads 6 against a floor of 10 with five cards named as uncounted; the goldfish models 3 of 9 draw cards. Both numbers are floors, which means the axis cannot currently carry a cut-or-add decision.
TWO LOGGED GAMES, 1W-1L, ON TWO DIFFERENT AND BOTH-SUPERSEDED LISTS (log 001 on sha 0480aaf7, log 002 on b394917f). Neither is evidence about V5, and the sample would not be evidence at any sha.
overall_assessment: This deck plays the critical-mass game (strategy:critical-mass: 'every card feeds one plan, and the plan is reaching the threshold where the synergies take over'), and V5 changed WHICH threshold. The old threshold was a combat event — an eight-mana 7/6 resolving and connecting, median turn 7 in the goldfish, with everything before it posture. The new threshold is a board state: an entry engine on the battlefield. Purphoros converts each entry into 2 damage at every seat and never touches your own board, and Molten Echoes converts each nontoken Dinosaur entry into a second entry; at the measured 2.02 entries per reveal that is roughly 4 damage per opponent per connect and 12 across the table, before casting, before tokens, before the copy layer. That is the change strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry has been asking this deck to make since it was first framed — 'wide alpha strikes, loops, commander-damage kills, and each-opponent drains are the payoffs that actually scale' against '~120 combined life behind three defenses' — and strategy:life-as-resource.philosophy-of-fire states the same law from the damage side: 'raw cards-to-damage math collapses against ~120 combined life — reach must scale (each-opponent drains, commander damage, damage doublers) or be held as targeted finishing rather than the plan.' Trading Chandra's Ignition for Purphoros is that law applied: Ignition off Gishath would kill 31 of the 34 other creatures in this 99 (enumerated from cards.json; only both Ghaltas and Zacama survive on toughness, and Purphoros itself would have survived on indestructible), which is a reset button in a deck whose plan is a wide board. A one-shot symmetrical seven becomes a repeatable asymmetric clock. Molten Echoes also draws a line the deck must now play around: CAST doors fire 'if you cast it' text and PUT doors do not, so Zacama's untap and Wakening Sun's Avatar's one-sided wipe exist off Descendants' Path, World War Hulk and prowl, and do not exist off the reveal, Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual or Savage Order. Against that, the cost: V5 spent its interaction budget. Removal COUNT is fine — deck-audit reads 9 against Walser's floor of 8 — but BREADTH is 3 classes of 5, with graveyard and land uncovered and exactly one artifact answer and one enchantment answer left in the 99 (Zacama's {2}{G} and Bronzebeak Foragers' ETB), both attached to creatures that must first resolve. strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite's own verdict on linear decks is that this is the bargain, not a defect — strategy:critical-mass calls interaction slots 'the price of the engine' and says the defence is 'speed, redundancy, and resilience, not answers' — but it prices the matchup: you cannot answer a lock piece, so you must outrun it. The deck is now honestly two clocks, one of which the table can only stop by answering an indestructible enchantment that is a creature only while your devotion to red is five or more (Purphoros is a 6/5 whose damage trigger does not care either way), and the pilot's job has shifted accordingly: the pivot to name is no longer 'Gishath connected' but 'an entry engine resolved', and per strategy:pivot-point recognising that a turn early is the whole skill. What is missing is measurement, not theory: Forge has never seen this list, the two logged games are on two superseded shas, and nothing in the stacks directory verifies a single V5 interaction.
gaps: NO SECTION ON ENTRY-COUNT ENGINES as a school — the Purphoros/Impact Tremors class, where the currency is permanents entering rather than spells cast or creatures attacking. strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry names 'each-opponent drains' as a payoff class in one clause and gives no arithmetic; strategy:critical-mass.storm-math is the nearest thing and its unit is a one-turn burst of spells — Girten's balance is 'enough cards in hand to cast sufficient spells in one turn' — which does not describe a permanent-entry count accumulated across turns by a trigger. This deck needed a threshold expressed in entries per turn and there is nowhere to cite it.

NO SECTION ON THE SYMMETRY OF YOUR OWN EFFECTS. The Chandra's Ignition to Purphoros swap is the general case — when a deck's plan is a wide board, a symmetrical sweeper is a cost, and the test is enumerable (how many of my own cards die to my own effect?). strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math covers the OPPONENT's wrath and says nothing about yours.

NO SECTION ON CAST-GATED vs PUT-GATED EFFECTS, or more generally on cheat-into-play as a strategic class distinct from cost reduction. A goldfish group can read 83.0% while the cards that answer the hard half — the ones that actually touch a command-zone cast — go unmeasured, and 'if you cast it' silently deletes half a card's text. The doc has nothing.

NO SECTION ON TYPAL/TRIBAL CONSTRUCTION: critical mass of a creature type, the typal-land tradeoff (Unclaimed Territory, Secluded Courtyard, Path of Ancestry), and what the off-type utility creature costs a typal payoff. Six of this deck's 35 creatures are not Dinosaurs and that is load-bearing for the reveal. Queried four ways; top hit was strategy:critical-mass.storm-math at 0.199.

NO SECTION ON TOP-OF-LIBRARY MANIPULATION as a setup discipline (Congregation at Dawn, Worldly Tutor, Descendants' Path, Bonehoard Dracosaur, Etali) — the reveal-and-cast school this deck's whole fuel layer belongs to. Top query hit was strategy:schools at 0.222.

NO SECTION ON COMMANDER-RELIANT CONSTRUCTION as a school. strategy:deckbuilding.archetype-selection draws the line in one sentence — 'built around your commander is not reliant on it' — and stops. What changes in mulligan rules, protection sizing and pivot timing when the commander is the only engine, and what changes back when a second engine is installed, is exactly what V5 did and there is no section that treats it.

NO SECTION ON READING A PRIOR-VERSION SIMULATION RECORD against a revised list: which figures survive fifteen swaps (the pod's clock, elimination sources, the connect rate) and which do not (engine casts, win rate). This frame cites a V3 connect rate of 0.70 to justify a V5 goldfish declaration and had to caveat it at every use.

NO SECTION ON WHEN A DECK SHOULD RUN TWO UNCONNECTED CLOCKS. strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density gets closest with Eisenherz's rule of two primary combos, 'a Plan A and Plan B', and the layering fix, but it is written about combo finishers, not about a combat clock and a noncombat drain running off the same resource.
